title: · In View | Hermès Unveils the 2026 Winter Windows and Holiday Light Installation at Maison Hermès Shanghai: Rising Toward the Void ·
original_title: 视野 | Hermès 揭幕上海爱马仕之家2026冬季橱窗和节日灯光装置：向空而生
excerpt: Hermès Shanghai unveiled its 2026 winter windows, "Growing Into Air," featuring Hungarian artist Zsófia Keresztes's glass mosaic sculptures inspired by nature's growth.
author: 撰稿 X Vivi 编辑 X RAN

blocks.text: On November 19, the Hermès Maison Shanghai unveiled its 2026 winter windows, this season themed "Growing Into Air" and created in collaboration with Hungarian artist Zsófia Keresztes. Drawing inspiration from nature's ingenuity, the artist uses glass mosaic sculptures to capture life's evolution from bud to wind-blown bloom, inviting viewers to sense the quiet strength gathered in dormancy and the moving beauty of life growing freely toward the open sky.

Based in Budapest, Zsófia Keresztes is known for her mosaic sculptures. Her work focuses on the evolution of life and the interconnectedness of all things, exploring the multidimensional interplay of the body, natural instinct, and emotional labor, and revealing both the fragility and resilience of life.
Zsófia Keresztes Contemporary Artist Born 1985 Nationality Hungarian Alma Mater Hungarian University of Fine Arts

By cutting and reassembling glass, Keresztes employs a pixelated visual language to interpret life's growth trajectory—curling inward and unfurling outward. Hand-set glass mosaics ripple across the sculptures' contours, shimmering softly as light shifts, while pink checkered butterfly nets woven from openwork fabric thread through the scene. In the women's windows, rain falls from the rims of bud-shaped umbrellas, and honeycomb openings connect a nurturing inner space with the unknown world beyond. Buds hang from above, breathing life into Hermès objects nestled among fringes.

The men's windows grow outward from a sheltered space. The cocoon-like structures draw inspiration from the delicate respiratory systems of insects, resting alongside forms that resemble wings and leaves. Roots and branches intersect freely, tracing naturally unfurling veins.
Enlarge view Click to enlarge for ultra-clear visuals

Strange plants hover within the accessories windows, symbolizing the many facets of sensory perception. Tableware serves as both the compound eyes of insects and blossoms on branches; ties cascade down as aerial roots, echoing the mosaics and checkered butterfly nets—a symbol of open, multidimensional observation.

The festive light installation at the entrance draws inspiration from the lively flutter of butterfly wings, evoking the natural spectacle of butterflies roosting together. Clustered around branches, the swarm rests close, coexisting in harmony and warming the atmosphere of holiday reunion. Flowing light and shadow trace life's journey from dormancy to transformation, telling a poetic tale of connection and renewal.
